source.title: Loft Board Requests in DOB NOW: Build service notice

passages.heading: PDF page 1
passages.text:
Yegal Shamash , PE, Acting Commissioner nyc.gov/buildings
build safe | live safe
January 8 , 20 2 6
SERVICE NOTICE
June 2010 Loft Board Requests in DOB NOW : Build
Starting on February 2 , 2026, Loft Board requests will be submitted in
DOB NOW: Build . Job filings on buildings with a Loft Law flag in the Property
Profile will not be approved until a Loft Board Request has been submitted
for review and a Letter of No Objection (LNO) or a Loft Board Certification has
been issued. The Loft Board will also review Certificate of Occupancy request .
Submit a Loft Board Request
Loft Board requests are always submitted in conjunction with a job filing (including Elevator
applications). Once the job filing is submitted, a Loft Board request is required to be added to the
filing for review .
• Go to the Loft Board tab and select +Add to create a new Loft Board request.
• The request is auto populated with the information entered on the job filing.
• The type of Loft Board submission will depend on the answer to the new question, Will the
proposed work take place in, or affect, an interim multiple dwelling (IMD) unit?
Answer Work Location Process
Yes In or affecting an IMD unit File for Loft Board Certification and include a
Narrative Statement
No
In a commercial unit and
does not affect an IMD
Unit
Request a Letter of No Objection from the Loft
Board
• Answer the questions about the IMD or Commercial units on the Scope of Work tab.
• Complete all required sections, including the Documents and S ignatures & Statement tabs.
Select Save and Submit the request for review .
DOB NOW Training
The NYC Department of Buildings is conducting free training sessions to explain the new process
and demonstrate how to navigate Loft Board requests in DOB NOW: Build . Visit the DOB NOW
Training Page at nyc.gov/dobnowtraining to regist er for training and to access user manuals
and training videos.
For additional assistance, submit an inquiry nyc.gov/dobnowhelp .
